name: Stroke
oneLine: A stroke is any unit of recognition - positive or negative, tied to what you did (conditional) or who you are (unconditional) - and any stroke beats no stroke at all.
whatYouDid: You sorted Dev's "you trained them well" into positive-and-conditional, then watched what happens once Rosita has to decide whether to let a stroke actually land or deflect it - the sorting only matters once that decision gets made.
confusion: People assume a stroke has to be positive to count; the tell is that negative strokes are still strokes, and most people will take a negative stroke over no stroke at all rather than go stroke-deprived.

fromBook.quote: A stroke is defined as a unit of recognition.

expand.definition: Strokes classify along two independent axes: positive/negative (pleasant or painful to receive) and conditional/unconditional (tied to behavior, or to identity) - any stroke can be any combination of the two.
expand.otherFraming: Steiner's Fuzzy Tale makes the same point as a fable: everyone starts out with an unlimited supply of Warm Fuzzies, until a bad witch teaches them to believe the supply is about to run out.
expand.tryThisToday: Give one unconditional positive stroke today ("good to have you around") instead of your usual conditional one ("nice work on that") and notice how differently it lands.
